games.name: Four in a Row
games.summary: Drop discs into a brass and walnut board and line up four before the house does.
games.intro: Seven columns, six rows, one brass board. Take the free preview for a spin against the house.
games.coverAlt: The Four in a Row board in brass and walnut
features: Easy and Medium opponents, and pass and play for two on one device
Hints and take-backs whenever you like
Tonight's Lamp: a fresh opening every day, the same for everyone
Short lessons from how discs fall to trapping the house with two threats at once
how: You are red, the house is ivory. Players alternate, one disc per turn.
A disc falls to the lowest empty slot of the column you choose.
Line up four of your colour, sideways, upright or on a diagonal, and you win.
No four and no room left? The game is drawn.
keys: Press 1 to 7, or Tab to a column, move with the arrow keys and press Enter.
Takes back your last disc and the house reply.
tips: Own the middle column early; it sits on the most lines.
Build two threats at once. A double threat cannot be blocked.
Mind the square above a threat: playing beneath it can hand over the win.
Medium looks several moves ahead, so set a trap rather than a straight line.

games.name: Hearts
games.tagline: Dodge the hearts, mind the Queen.
games.summary: Pass three, dodge the hearts, and think twice before you take the Queen of Spades. First to 100 loses.
games.intro: Four seats, thirteen cards each, one match to 100. Sit South and try the free preview.
games.coverAlt: Hearts at the baize table on a tablet
features: You and three computer opponents at Easy and Medium
Every legal card is shown; hints say why a play is good
Pass left, right, across or hold, then shoot the moon if you dare
Short lessons, one idea at a time
how: Everyone gets 13 cards. Before play, pass three to a neighbour: left, right, across, then hold with no pass.
The 2 of clubs starts the first trick. Follow suit when you can.
Highest card of the led suit wins the trick and leads next.
No hearts and no Queen of spades on the first trick, unless you hold nothing else.
Hearts may not lead until one has been played.
Each heart costs 1 point and the Queen of spades costs 13. Fewer is better.
Take every heart and the Queen to shoot the moon: you score 0 and the others take 26.
The match ends when someone reaches 100; the lowest score wins.
keys: Tap a card to play it. Dimmed cards are not legal.
Tab into your hand, arrow keys to move, Enter or Space to play.
Pick three cards, then Pass cards. Hint suggests three.
Hint explains a good play. Undo takes back your last card.
tips: Pass the Queen of spades and the high spades unless you hold plenty of small ones to guard them.
Slip under the winning card whenever you can.
Shedding a big heart or the Queen on a trick you cannot win is the heart of the game.
games.metaDescription: Play Hearts free against three computer opponents in your browser: pass three, shoot the moon, first to 100 loses. The full game is coming soon to the App Store and Google Play.

games.name: Hex
games.summary: Join your two shores with a chain of sea-glass stones on a limestone tide table. Someone always wins.
games.intro: A limestone slab, shallow hollows and teal and amber sea-glass stones under a hanging lamp. Link your two shores before your rival does.
games.coverAlt: The Hex board: a limestone slab with teal and amber stones
features: Play the house at three levels, or hand the device to a friend
An 11 by 11 board, or a quicker 9 by 9
A swap rule you can switch on, so the first move stays fair
A hint with the reason behind it, and take-backs
Four short lessons: connecting, blocking ladders, bridges and the swap
A daily position: win it in a few stones
how: Teal links the west and east shores; amber links north and south.
Players take turns placing one stone on any empty hollow. Stones never move or leave.
The first side to complete an unbroken chain between its two shores wins.
A game never ends in a draw: when the board is full, exactly one side has a chain.
With the swap rule on, the second player may take over the first stone instead of replying.
tips: The centre is worth more than the edge: start near it.
Two stones with two shared empty hollows between them are linked, even if the rival cuts one.
Blocking from a distance usually beats blocking up close.

games.name: Dots and Boxes
games.tagline: Thread the pegs, seal the squares.
games.summary: Stretch silk threads between enamel pegs on a linen cloth and close boxes with wax seals.
games.intro: Vermilion and indigo silk threads, enamel pegs on linen, and a wax seal for every box you close.
games.coverAlt: Dots and Boxes on a linen cloth with silk threads
features: Play the house at three levels, or pass and play
Cloths in three sizes: 4 by 4, 5 by 5 and 6 by 6 boxes
A needle hint that shows a safe thread and tells you why
Four short lessons: boxes, safe moves, chains and the double-cross
A daily endgame puzzle
how: Players take turns stretching one thread between two neighbouring pegs.
Complete the fourth side of a box and a wax seal marks it as yours.
Closing a box earns another turn, so keep going while you can.
When every thread is placed, the player with more boxes wins.
tips: Avoid giving the third side of a box: it hands your rival a seal.
Near the end the board splits into chains. Count them before you commit.
Sometimes it pays to decline the last two boxes of a chain to keep control.

games.name: Yacht
games.summary: Five tinted glass dice, three rolls a turn and an ink score card to fill. Chase a high score or beat the house.
games.intro: Throw five glass dice, keep the ones you like and write the best line on an ink score card.
games.coverAlt: Yacht: glass dice beside an ink score card
features: Solo score chase, a game against the computer, or two players
Twelve categories and an upper-section bonus, with a preview of each line before you write it
A coach hint that weighs the odds and explains its choice
Hold, re-roll and undo before you commit
Short lessons on holding, choosing a line, the bonus and risk
A daily game with the same dice for everyone
how: Throw all five dice. You may keep any and re-roll the rest, twice.
After your last roll, write the result on one empty line of the card.
Upper lines (Aces to Sixes) add up matching dice; reach 63 there for a 35 point bonus.
Lower lines pay for Choice, Four of a Kind, Full House, straights and Yacht, five of a kind.
When all twelve lines are filled, the card is complete and the total is your score.
tips: Early on, chase the upper lines that make the 63 bonus reachable.
A line you cannot fill is not wasted if you spend it on a poor roll.
Keep pairs for a Full House or Four of a Kind; keep runs for straights.

games.name: Liar's Dice
games.tagline: Bid, bluff and call by candlelight.
games.summary: Hidden dice under glazed ceramic cups, three rivals with their own habits, and a candle in the middle of the table.
games.intro: Everyone shakes dice under a cup. Bid how many of a face are on the table, and call the bluff when you do not believe it.
games.coverAlt: Liar's Dice: three ceramic cups around a candle
features: You against three rivals: Ash is careful, Ember bluffs and Cinder leaps at the count
Ones can be wild, or play with plain dice
A full game of five dice each, or a quick game of three
A hint that gives the odds and says why
Short lessons on odds, bidding, bluffing and wild ones
A daily round with the same dice for everyone
how: Each player shakes their dice under a cup and looks at their own.
In turn, raise the bid: more dice, or the same number of a higher face.
Instead of raising you may call. Every cup is lifted and the claim is counted.
If the table holds at least as many as claimed, the caller loses a die. If not, the bidder does.
Lose all your dice and you are out. The last cup standing wins.
tips: Start from what is in your own cup: it is the only evidence you have.
Opening a little low gives nothing away.
Learn how each rival bids before you decide whom to doubt.

games.name: Filament
games.tagline: One glowing loop, every number met.
games.summary: A loop puzzle in glass and light. Draw one closed wire through the pegs so every clue number is satisfied.
games.intro: Light a single closed loop through a grid of pegs. Each number says how many sides of its cell the wire uses.
games.coverAlt: Filament: a glowing loop on a smoked-glass plate
features: Fresh puzzles generated for every game, each with exactly one solution
Easy, Medium and Hard, from 5 by 5 up to 10 by 10
Hints that explain the deduction, not just the answer
A pen for marking strands that are not part of the loop
Four short lessons: reading numbers, zeros and threes, corners and pegs, one loop only
A daily puzzle with the same grid for everyone, and a lamp that lights when you finish
how: Draw one closed loop through the pegs, moving along the grid lines.
A number in a cell says how many of its four sides the loop uses.
Cells without a number are free. The loop never crosses or branches.
When the loop closes and every number is met, the lamp lights.
tips: Start with the zeros and threes: they place strands straight away.
A corner peg has only two strands, so a loop that touches it takes both.
Close a loop too early and the numbers left outside cannot be met.
